obligation: Internal notice from the group SOC to each affected division
trigger: The SOC declares a Severity 1 incident involving bench workstations, the STPP, retail lanes, or IT Support field devices
deadline: Immediately on the incident bridge
notify: Device Repair CISO; Electronics Retail CISO; IT Support security and compliance lead and Privacy Official
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - group policy

obligation: Acquirer notice of suspected card data compromise (retail merchant account)
citation: Retail merchant agreement (fictional term); PCI DSS v4.0.1 Requirement 12.10.1 (N44-45-R01)
trigger: Suspected compromise of brand card data on retail POS lanes, including a common point of purchase notice from the acquirer
deadline: Within 24 hours of suspecting a compromise. The clock starts at suspicion, not confirmation
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not law
notifying_entity: Electronics Retail (payments director with the Electronics Retail CISO)

obligation: Acquirer notice of suspected card data compromise (repair merchant account)
citation: Repair merchant agreement (fictional term); PCI DSS v4.0.1 Requirement 12.10.1 (N81-R03)
trigger: Suspected compromise of card data taken by Device Repair (P2PE terminals, booking page, phone payments)
deadline: Within 24 hours of suspecting a compromise
notify: Acquirer for the repair merchant account
applies_at_this_tier: Only if repair card data is suspected. In the exercise scenario forensics found no effect on P2PE terminals or the booking page by Day 2; counsel documents that conclusion
notifying_entity: Device Repair (chief financial officer with the Device Repair CISO)

obligation: Card brand compromise procedures, including a PCI Forensic Investigator if required
citation: Payment brand operating rules, applied through the acquirer (not law)
trigger: The acquirer or a card brand opens a compromise case
deadline: Per acquirer and brand instructions (not verified in this sample)
notify: Acquirer; card brands through the acquirer
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - follow acquirer instructions; brand rules were not verified

obligation: Manufacturer A notice of a suspected incident involving customer data or devices
citation: Manufacturer A authorized service provider agreement (fictional term)
trigger: Suspected incident involving customer data or devices at an authorized location
deadline: Within 24 hours of suspicion
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not law
notifying_entity: Device Repair (vice president of partner programs)

obligation: Manufacturer B notice of a suspected incident
citation: Manufacturer B warranty depot agreement (fictional term)
trigger: Suspected incident at the 3 warranty depots
deadline: Within 24 hours of suspicion
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not law (3 depots ran the compromised tool)

obligation: TPA notice of a security incident affecting plan holders' data
trigger: Security incident affecting plan holders' data held for claims (ticket records and devices in for plan repairs)
deadline: Within 48 hours (contract term)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not law
notifying_entity: Device Repair (vice president of partner programs)

obligation: Third-party agent notice from Device Repair to the TPA (state law)
citation: Fla. Stat. 501.171(6)(a) (worked example; other states' third-party agent duties vary) (N81-R02)
trigger: Breach of a system Device Repair maintains with plan holders' personal information on the TPA's behalf
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 10 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred, with all information the TPA needs to notify. The 48-hour contract term is shorter and is met first
notify: TPA (the covered entity for its plan holders)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - for plan holders' records the division maintains for the TPA

obligation: Enterprise depot customer notice
trigger: Security incident affecting a business account's devices or data
deadline: Within 72 hours after the division confirms the incident
notify: Each affected business account's designated contact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not law

obligation: Business associate notice to covered entities (IT Support)
trigger: Breach of unsecured PHI at a practice workstation an IT Support technician diagnosed with the compromised tool (presumed unless the 164.402 assessment shows a low probability of compromise)
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery; the BAAs shorten this to 10 calendar days (standard) or 5 business days (47 practices). Include each affected individual's identity to the extent possible (164.410(c)(1))
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - IT Support is a business associate of 610 practices; 14 practices are in scope in the exercise
clock_starts: Discovery: first day known, or by reasonable diligence would have been known, to any employee or agent (164.410(a)(2))

obligation: Covered entities' own breach notices (practices)
trigger: Each practice decides its own breach determination and notices to individuals, HHS, and media
deadline: Practices' duty, not the group's: individuals no later than 60 days after discovery; HHS and media by the 500-person rules
applies_at_this_tier: Not the group's duty. IT Support supports the practices with facts and individual lists

obligation: Managed services customer notice (non-HIPAA customers)
trigger: Security incident affecting a managed customer's systems or data
deadline: Within 72 hours after the division confirms the incident
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not law

obligation: Third-party agent notice from IT Support to managed customers (state law)
trigger: Breach of a system IT Support maintains with a customer's personal information
deadline: No later than 10 days after determination; the 72-hour contract term is met first
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - where IT Support maintains customers' personal information

obligation: FTC Safeguards Rule notification event (customers that are financial institutions)
trigger: Unauthorized acquisition of unencrypted customer information of 500 or more consumers at an accounting or tax firm customer
deadline: Customer's duty: as soon as possible and no later than 30 days after discovery
applies_at_this_tier: Not the group's duty (the group is not a financial institution). IT Support gives affected firms the facts they need
notifying_entity: Affected accounting and tax firm customers

obligation: State data breach notification (all affected individuals)
citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48) (N81-R02)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information of residents: card numbers with security codes and names; user name or email with a password; medical, geolocation, or other data elements where a state covers them
deadline: Varies by state (for example without unreasonable delay or a fixed number of days)
notify: Affected residents; state attorney general or regulator where required; consumer reporting agencies above state-set counts
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - apply the law of each of the 26 states where affected individuals reside
notifying_entity: Device Repair; Electronics Retail; IT Support (each as the covered entity for its own customers)

obligation: Florida notice to individuals (worked example)
trigger: Breach of personal information of Florida residents: account email and password pairs from ticket notes, card numbers with security codes, and device content such as medical or geolocation information (501.171(1)(g))
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred. 15 more days are available for this notice only if good cause is given in writing to the Department within the 30 days (501.171(3)(a))
notify: Each affected Florida resident (mail or email; substitute notice if over 500,000 people or $250,000 cost)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - expected for each division's Florida customers in the exercise
notifying_entity: Device Repair; Electronics Retail; IT Support

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs (worked example)
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination (no extension for this notice)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (synopsis, number of Floridians, services offered, copy of the notice, contact)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - each notifying division with 500 or more Florida residents

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies (worked example)
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies (timing, distribution, and content of the notices)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Device Repair and Electronics Retail in the exercise

obligation: Florida law enforcement delay (worked example)
trigger: A law enforcement agency determines that notice would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay for the period the agency specifies in its written request
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if requested

obligation: Florida no-notice determination (worked example)
trigger: After investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the entity reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Document the determination, keep it 5 years, and give it to the Department within 30 days after the determination
applies_at_this_tier: Possible only for tickets with no passcode or credential and no device content accessed; counsel decides

obligation: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05 (material cybersecurity incident)
trigger: The registrant determines a cybersecurity incident is material
deadline: 4 business days after the materiality determination (delay only on a U.S. Attorney General determination)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Cris Santos Company Holdings is an SEC registrant
clock_starts: Materiality determination, made without unreasonable delay

obligation: SEC Reg S-K Item 106 annual disclosure
trigger: Annual report
deadline: Next Form 10-K
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - lessons from the incident may inform the risk management and governance description

obligation: Voluntary report to law enforcement and CISA
trigger: Suspected criminal compromise of a software supplier, card data, and customer devices
deadline: As soon as practicable (target Day 0 to Day 1)
notify: FBI (IC3) or U.S. Secret Service field office; CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Recommended; supports a law enforcement delay request and OFAC mitigation

obligation: Tool vendor coordination
citation: Bench tool license terms (no security terms today; POAM-008)
trigger: The group confirms the vendor's update channel delivered malicious code
deadline: Immediately; request indicators and the vendor's own incident timeline
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - not a legal duty; needed for scoping

obligation: Cyber insurance claim notice
trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy; call the carrier hotline before engaging vendors
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not law

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any extortion payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: An extortion demand (for example a threat to publish stolen device content)
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Only if an extortion demand is made. All U.S. persons
notifying_entity: Group (Group General Counsel; board risk committee approval under POL-03 4.7)

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after a ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: NOT YET REQUIRED: final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; reporting is voluntary until then

obligation: HIPAA breach notification as a covered entity
trigger: Breach of unsecured PHI held by a covered entity
deadline: n/a
applies_at_this_tier: No - no division is a covered entity; IT Support's duty as a business associate is the 164.410 row above

obligation: Covered telecommunications or Kaspersky covered article discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-25(d) and FAR 52.204-23(c); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies covered equipment or a Kaspersky covered article
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification for covered telecommunications equipment or services (52.204-25(d)); within 3 business days for a Kaspersky covered article (52.204-23(c)); further report within 10 business days in both cases. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - the group holds no federal contracts (P03)
